samples.identification: Concealed Edge command download and result callback reconstruction
execution_trace: Lines 2-5 force-kill Edge and delete wildcard .000/.tmp/.crdownload files from Downloads to prepare the staging directory.

Line 6 launches Edge with a 1x1 window at 10000,10000 and disables certificate checks. Its Base64 HTML decodes to fetch(URL).then(r=>r.blob()).then(blob=>{ create anchor; assign URL.createObjectURL(blob); assign .000 filename; click anchor; }). The decoded URL is the same webhook.site endpoint used for the result upload.
Lines 7-8 wait ten seconds then copy /b Downloads/*.000 into TEMP/task.cmd. Wildcard copy can join matching files; the command does not authenticate or inspect downloaded code.
Line 9 runs that same task.cmd through cmd /c; stdout and stderr go to TEMP/result.txt. Line 10 curl -k --data-binary @TEMP/result.txt posts that same result file to the remote endpoint.
Line 11 deletes the staged command and its output. There is one fetch/run/report cycle, with no polling or persistence.
samples.verdict_balance: Concealed browser delivery, unverified remote shell code, and returning its output outweigh ordinary browser automation explanations. No package, release/version, authorization, or deployment context was supplied; repository evidence identifies a functional attack reconstruction, not a recovered actor-specific implant.
limits: The response payload is absent; no credential theft, ransomware, or additional commands are inferred.
Runtime success depends on Edge, download policy/CORS, endpoint contents, ten-second timing, paths and curl availability. Neither the sample nor its remote endpoint was executed/contacted.
The third-party mock-service signature matches @echo off plus webhook.site and size; it does not corroborate actor attribution or the malware verdict.

samples.identification: Loopback WebDAV NTLM capture proof of concept, New-Object variant
execution_trace: Line 1 constructs HttpListener; lines 2-3 add and start a loopback-only HTTP prefix.

Line 4 starts a background PowerShell job running net use f: against the same loopback host/port using the WebDAV UNC form. The c$ component does not prove an SMB admin-share connection, remote movement, or elevated execution.

Line 5 supplies a Base64 NTLMSSP type-2 message: 48 bytes, flags 0xa2898205, fixed server challenge 1122334455667788, empty target name/info. VERSION and TARGET_INFO flags are set but the message contains no version field or target-info payload; this synthetic challenge is not evidence of a successful handshake.

Lines 6-14 synchronously accept four requests, record any Authorization header, and return 401 with WWW-Authenticate: NTLM plus the fixed challenge. New-Object variant uses Add-Content -Value; constructor variant pipes the same header to Out-File -Append.

After four requests, Stop closes the listener. GetContext can wait indefinitely if fewer arrive. There is no message-type check: negotiation headers and other Authorization values may also be recorded, so a log entry alone proves neither capture of a usable NTLM response nor a password.
samples.verdict_balance: The script deliberately induces a local authentication exchange and records credential-bearing headers rather than validating a user or serving content. It is an attack proof of concept; authorized security testing could explain possession, but no such deployment context was supplied. Loopback limits reach, not the authentication-capture purpose.
limits: Listener registration rights, WebClient availability, the synthetic challenge and Windows policy can prevent capture. No runtime success is asserted.
No NTLM relay, name-resolution poisoning, privilege escalation, cracking, persistence, or external exfiltration exists in the traced code.

Coverage gap: one hostile capture and one suspicious coercion finding are justified. These represent distinct actions; there is no independent further hostile behavior to add without duplication or invention.

changes.change: Add notable structured call detection for standard background-job creation, scoped to PowerShell. Comments and strings are not calls; case-insensitive cmdlet spelling is accepted.
changes.placement: process/create/eval: standard Start-Job executes supplied PowerShell source in a background execution context.
changes.consumer_audit: Four ancestor consumers: both Empire rules and Android package rule exclude PowerShell by type. ComputerDefaults composite also requires registry write, ComputerDefaults target and shell-open association; adding a job call supplies only the existing neutral process-launch role.

changes.change: Override inherited T1187,T1557.001 with T1187. Direct loopback WebDAV coercion and header logging establish neither name-resolution poisoning nor relay. All matchers, severities, consumers and detection populations are retained.

verification.variant_controls: All 19 pre-existing ntlm-browser-variants fixtures statically scanned, plus three background-job fixtures. Existing hostile/suspicious behavior and benign boundaries retained. Background-job creation is notable; source references and Start-ThreadJob do not match. A mixed-case Start-Job control also matches.
verification.classifier_disagreement: Both PowerShell files remain ML BENIGN at calibrated level -1 despite hostile credential-capture findings. Their probabilities rise from 0.985709/0.9864824 to 0.98853564/0.98905057. This is a classifier coverage gap, not justification for extra or inaccurate traits. The model warns of v18/v19 feature-spec skew; its causal contribution is unproven.
verification.engine_note: Installed atomscan and PATH cleave contain an older directory-budget policy. After initial scan load failure, scans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 only to bypass that stale linter; full rule matching remained enabled. Final make validate uses the current /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/target/release/cleave, whose source explicitly admits the reviewed 101-rule naming budget.
